title.title: Finite generation for the $K(n)$-local sphere
title.subtitle: Claim: every $\pi_t L_{K(n)} S$ is a finitely generated $\mathbb Z_p$-module, at every prime and height

plain: The field's central object has endlessly complex layers; each one is still built from finitely many pieces

object.heading: Is $\pi_t L_{K(n)}S$ finitely generated over $\mathbb Z_p$? A window of the table
object.caption: rows: height $n = 1$ to $4$ · columns: $p = 2, 3, 5, 7$ · grey: known before

beats.text: Each cell: one prime $p$ and one chromatic height $n$
Known before: height 1, and height 2 for $p \ge 5$ (Shimomura's computations)
The claim fills the whole table, every prime and every height

steps: Compute each group with a descent spectral sequence
Past a fixed line, everything vanishes at a finite stage
So each degree has only finitely many generators

achievement.label: Hovey–Strickland Problem 16.2
statement: \pi_t L_{K(n)} S_p \ \text{is a finitely generated } \mathbb Z_p\text{-module}
achievement.context: With the known rational answer (Barthel–Schlank–Stapleton–Weinstein) this pins down the free ranks
achievement.note: No uniform bound on the torsion

verify.detail: Manuscript only: 103 pages, via a descent spectral sequence with a vanishing line
verify.ourCheck: We read the proof outline; we did not check the proof

voice.text: Each cell is a prime and a height. Before, only a corner was known.
A descent spectral sequence dies past a fixed line, so finitely many pieces.
Claimed: every group is finitely generated.

sources.quote: Hovey-Strickland Problem 16.2 and Hovey's problem list Problem 1. Height 1 classical; height 2, p >= 5 via Shimomura's computations

sources.quote: which together with the known rational computation of Barthel, Schlank, Stapleton and Weinstein pins down the free ranks
